attacks.claim: TRAILING_PUNCT is applied to each matched URL run, and the description has no length cap. A description with "https://" followed by a long run of punctuation and then a non-punctuation character makes the anchored `[...]+$` regex retry from every position, which is quadratic. Every viewer's item page would freeze during render, and the owner can trigger this.
The PR says truncation never splits a word, but the fallback branch cuts an unbroken text run mid-word at the limit. The test encodes that behaviour, so the stated contract and the code disagree.
attacks.evidence: else if (out.length === 0) out.push({ kind: 'text', value: Array.from(t.value).slice(0, limit).join('') }); ... expect(truncate(tokenize('x'.repeat(400)), 280).tokens).toEqual([{ kind: 'text', value: 'x'.repeat(280) }]);

attacks.claim: Trailing ')' is always stripped, so a Wikipedia-style URL with balanced parentheses, such as .../Foo_(bar), becomes a link to a truncated URL. The visible link text and the href are both wrong.

Neighbors' arbitrary external links render with no warning or destination preview. The display text is the raw string while href is the normalized URL, so an IDN or lookalike host can display differently from where it goes. This is a phishing surface, but it is a product-level risk and not a crash-level one.
attacks.evidence: return { kind: 'link', value: raw, href: url.href };
